questions.question: During the Sultanate of Delhi, the term "Ulema" was associated with ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Learned theologians and Jurists**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The term **"Ulema"** refers to a **group of Muslim scholars** who are recognized as having specialist knowledge of **Islamic sacred law and theology**.
 
• During the **Sultanate of Delhi**, as in other **Muslim societies,** they played a crucial role in interpreting and maintaining religious laws, teaching and advising on religious matters.
 
• They were not associated with **military, revenue, or postal roles.​**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• The Delhi Sultanate was a Muslim kingdom.
 
• Five dynasties ruled over the Delhi Sultanate sequentially: the** Mamluk/Slave dynasty (1206–1290), the Khilji dynasty (1290–1320), the Tughlaq dynasty (1320–1414), the Sayyid dynasty (1414–51), and the Lodi dynasty (1451–1526).**
 
• The sultanate is noted for its integration of the Indian subcontinent into a global cosmopolitan culture that extended from Spain in the west to Indonesia in the southeast.
 
• This involved the assimilation and fusion of varied influences, from Persian to Turkic and Arabic, as well as the indigenous cultures of the region.
 
• The period also saw significant **economic and demographic changes, including urbanization, the growth of trade, and the movement of large numbers of people from the region of Persia and Central Asia.**
 
• The Delhi Sultanate was often at war with neighboring kingdoms and confronted numerous** revolts, insurrections, and episodes of factional infighting.**
 
• **The Delhi Sultanate** ended in **1526**, when it was defeated by **Babur, the founder of the Mughal Empire, at the First Battle of Panipat.**

questions.question: Which plant tissue is responsible for the transportation of water and minerals from the soil to the stems and leaves?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Xylem**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Xylem:** 

 
 
• This is the **vascular tissue** in **plants** that conducts water and dissolved nutrients upward from the root and also helps to form the woody element in the stem. 
 
• The main function of **xylem **is to **transport water,** but it also transports some nutrients through the plant.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Parenchyma:**

 
 
• This is the most common type of **plant tissue **found in the **soft parts of plants.**
 
• It is responsible for the **plant's metabolic functions, such as photosynthesis, storage of starch, fats and oils, and helps in the healing and repair of wounds.**
 
 
 
• **Collenchyma:**
 
 
• This tissue gives support to the plant and is usually found in** layers beneath the epidermis**.
 
• **Collenchyma cells** are elongated cells with thickened cell walls that provide structure and **support for the plant, particularly in regions of new growth**.
 
 
 
• **Phloem:**
 
 
• This is the** living tissue** that transports the** soluble organic compounds made during photosynthesis and known as photosynthates, in particular, sugar, from leaves to the rest of the plant where needed.**
 
• This process is called **translocation**.

questions.question: Who was the court poet of Harshavardhana?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Banabhatta**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Banabhatta: **
 
• He was a Sanskrit scholar and** poet of India in the 7th century.** 
 
• He was the Asthana Kavi, meaning **Court Poet, of Harshavardhana, a notable emperor in North India in the early 7th century.** 
 
• He is the author of Harshacharita, a biography of his patron king Harshavardhana, and Kadambari, a romantic novel.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sri Ponna:**

 
 
• He was a **Kannada poet** in the court of** Rashtrakuta Dynasty King Krishna III**.
 
• He was one of the three gems of Kannada literature along with **Adikavi Pampa and Ranna.**
 
• Sri Ponna was given the title** "Emperor among poets" (Kavichakravarthi)** for his contributions to **Kannada literature.**
 
 
 
• **Parmanand**:
 
 
• In the context of Indian literature, Parmanand could refer to a 15th–16th-century saint and poet who wrote in the tradition of the **Bhakti movement, devotional literature that focused on personal connection to the divine.**
 
• His work is not associated with **Harshavardhana,** as he lived several centuries after the king's reign.

questions.question: Which is the oldest tennis tournament in the world?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Wimbledon**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Wimbledon:** 

 
 
• **The Championships, Wimbledon,** commonly known simply as Wimbledon, is the** oldest tennis tournament in the world,** and it is considered the most prestigious. 
 
• It has been held at the** All England Club** in **Wimbledon, London, since 1877.** 
 
• **Wimbledon** takes place over two weeks in late **June** and early **July.** 
 
• It is the only major tournament still played on grass, which is the game's original surface.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Australian Open: **

 
 
• **The Australian Open** is one of the **four Grand Slam tennis tournaments**.
 
• It is held annually in** Melbourne, Australia,** in the last two weeks of** January.**
 
• The tournament was first held in **1905,** making it the** youngest of the four Grand Slam events.**
 
 
 
• **French Open:**
 
 
• Also known as **Roland-Garros**, this is another of the **four annual Grand Slam tournaments.**
 
• It is held in **Paris, France, over two weeks in late May and early June.**
 
• The French Open was established in **1891**, making it the third oldest of the four Grand Slam tournaments.
 
 
 
• **US Open: **
 
 
• **The US Open** is held annually in** late August and early September **over a two-week period in **New York City, United States.**
 
• The US Open originated from two separate tournaments: the men's tournament which started in** 1881 and the women's tournament which started in 1887.**

questions.question: Which union territory has a high court of its own?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Delhi**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Delhi High Court was established on **31st October 1966.**
 
• The High Court of Delhi was established with **four judges, including the Chief Justice K.S.Hegde from Mysore High Court (now Karnataka High Court). ​**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Indian judiciary is a hierarchy of courts with the **Supreme Court at the top, followed by High Courts for each state or group of states, and subordinate courts at the local level. **
 
• **Supreme Court:**
 
 
• **The Supreme Court of India **is the** highest judicial forum and final court of appeal under the Constitution of India.**
 
• It is composed of the **Chief Justice of India and a maximum of 33 other judges.**
 
• The Supreme Court has o**riginal, appellate, and advisory jurisdiction.**
 
 
 
• **High Courts:**
 
 
• Each state has a **High Court** which is the highest court within that state's jurisdiction. 
 
 
 
• **Subordinate Courts:**
 
 
• Below the** High Courts **are a hierarchy of subordinate courts including** District Courts, Family Courts, Labour Court, Industrial Tribunal, and others.**
 
• These courts deal with** civil and criminal matters of state and local levels.**
 
 
 
• **Tribunals:**
 
 
• Apart from the regular hierarchy of courts, there are several tribunals established in India for various** matters, including Income Tax, Customs, Excise, Armed Forces, Consumer Disputes, etc.**
 
• While these tribunals aren't part of the **traditional judicial structure, they play a key role in the Indian justice system.**

questions.question: Cells were first observed in cork by ______ in 1665.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Robert Hooke**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Robert Hooke:**

 
 
• **Robert Hooke** was an** English scientist in the 17th century who is often credited with first observing cells.**
 
• He used a **microscope** to observe the structure of **a thin cutting of cork **and noticed it was made up of **tiny, hollow compartments which he called "cells" because they reminded him of the cells of a monastery.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Theophrastus:**

 
 
• Known as the** "Father of Botany,"** Theophrastus was a Greek philosopher who studied under Plato and Aristotle.
 
• He is credited with major contributions to botany and biology, but he lived in the 4th century BC, well before the discovery of cells.
 
 
 
• **Edward Jenner:**
 
 
• Edward Jenner was an **English physician** and scientist who was the pioneer of smallpox vaccine, the world's first vaccine.
 
• While his work was instrumental in the field of immunology, he was not involved in the initial discovery of cells.
 
 
 
• **Anton van Leeuwenhoek:**
 
 
• Anton van Leeuwenhoek, a **Dutch scientist from the 17th century,** is considered the "Father of Microbiology."
 
• He greatly improved the microscope and was the first to document the existence of **bacteria, protists, sperm cells, and blood cells.**
 
• While he did significant work with microscopic observations, he did not first observe cells in cork - that was Hooke.

questions.question: Which harvest festival is famously celebrated in Assam?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bhogali Bihu**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bhogali Bihu:** 

 
 
• This is a **harvest festival celebrated in Assam, a state in northeastern India.** 
 
• Also known as **Magh Bihu**, it marks the end of the harvesting season in the month of Maagha (January-February). 
 
• It involves community feasts and bonfires.
 
• **Bihu **is a set of three important Assamese festivals in the calendar year: **Bhogali (Makar Sankranti), Rongali or Bohag Bihu (Assamese New Year, usually mid-April), and Kongali Bihu (October-November, no specific date).**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lohri:**

 
 
• Lohri is a Punjabi festival celebrated primarily by people from the Punjab region of South Asia.
 
• It marks the end of winter and is traditionally associated with the harvest of the rabi crops.
 
• The day is celebrated with a bonfire, singing, dancing, and a feast.
 
 
 
• **Makar Sankranti:**
 
 
• This festival is a pan-Indian solar festival observed in the month of January.
 
• It marks the transition of the sun into the zodiacal sign of Makara (Capricorn) on its celestial path, which is the first change in the zodiac after the winter solstice.
 
• It signifies the arrival of longer days. Makar Sankranti is known by different names in different parts of India and is associated with many customs, which are usually related to the harvest.
 
 
 
• **Onam**:
 
 
• Onam is a harvest festival celebrated in Kerala, a state in South India.
 
• It is the biggest and the most important festival of the state and is celebrated with numerous festivities such as Vallam Kali (boat races), Pulikali (tiger dances), Pookkalam (flower Rangoli), Onathappan (worship), and other celebrations.

questions.question: Ustad Shafaat Ahmed Khan was best known for which of the following instrument?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is** Tabla**. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Tabla:**
 
• The Tabla is a percussive instrument consisting of a pair of hand drums used in the **traditional, classical, popular, and folk music of the Indian subcontinent.**
 
• It has been important in** Hindustani classical music since the 18th century and remains in use today.**
 
• **Ustad Shafaat Ahmed Khan** was a renowned Indian classical musician known for his virtuosity on the **tabla.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rudra Veena**:

 
 
• The Rudra Veena is a plucked string instrument used in **Hindustani classical music.**
 
• One of the oldest instruments in the world, the Rudra Veena is not as commonly played today but is revered for its deep, meditative sound.
 
 
 
• **Harmonium:**
 
 
• The Harmonium is a keyboard instrument that uses a** hand-pumped bellows to produce sound.**
 
• It is commonly used in Indian classical and folk music, as well as in popular music.
 
 
 
• **Violin**:
 
 
• The Violin is a **stringed instrument that is played with a bow.**
 
• It originated in Italy in the 16th century and has since been adopted worldwide.
 
• In Indian classical music, it has been adapted as a solo instrument, and it's widely used in Hindustani as well as in Carnatic music.

questions.question: Which state government launched the "Panchamrut Yojana"?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Uttar Pradesh**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Uttar Pradesh government **announced that **Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath's 'Panchamrut Yojana'** will aid in doubling farmers' income through the implementation of cost-effective technical measures and the promotion of co-cropping.
 
• An official from the Sugarcane Development Department has announced that the government has already begun implementing the Panchamrut Yojana.
 
• The first phase of the plan will include 2028 farmers, selected to create model farms.
 
• The goal is to encourage other farmers to join in, seeing the benefits firsthand.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• A press release from the UP government explains the** Panchamrut scheme's goals.**
 
• It aims to cut down the cost of growing **sugarcane, boost the quantity produced, and make the soil healthier.**
 
• It does this by using five methods: a special way of planting sugarcane, managing old crop stalks, using crop waste as mulch, efficient watering, and growing different crops together.
 
• The plan hopes to cut costs by saving water and making the most of **crop leftovers, reducing the need for fertilizers and pesticides.**
 
• It promotes growing more than one type of crop to boost overall production.
 
• This scheme will also increase farmers' earnings and help control pollution by removing the need to burn leftover crop parts in the fields.

questions.question: How many field players are in a hockey team?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**11**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In field hockey, each team typically consists of **11 players: 10 outfield players and 1 goalkeeper.**
 
• However, the exact number can vary slightly depending on the specific rules of a given **league or tournament**.
 
• **Hockey** is a fast-paced sport played between two teams, traditionally of six players each: one goaltender and five players who skate up and down the ice trying to take the puck and score goals against the opposing team.
 
• There are different types of hockey including** ice hockey, field hockey, roller hockey, sledge hockey, and street hockey, among others. Here, I'll focus on ice hockey, the most globally recognized type.​**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ice hockey **is typically played on a rectangular rink with rounded corners.
 
• The rink is divided into three sections: **two end zones (where the goals are located) and a neutral zone in between**.
 
• The end zones contain a goal crease, a semi-circular area in front of the goal where specific rules apply.
 
• The objective of the game is to score more goals than the opposing team
 
• A goal is scored when the puck completely crosses the goal line between the posts and under the crossbar of the opposing team's goal.

questions.question: The reaction between an acid and a base is known as _____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Neutralisation reaction.​**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

**__Neutralisation__**

__
 
• **The ionic compound that results from the neutralization reaction of an acid and a base is called Salt.**
 
• It can be defined as a chemical reaction in which an acid reacts with a base to produce salt along with water.
 
• **The reaction of an acid with a base is called a neutralization reaction.**
 
• The products of this reaction are salt and water.
 
• For example, the reaction of hydrochloric acid(HCl) with sodium hydroxide(NaOH) produces a solution of sodium chloride(NaCl)(salt) and some additional water molecules.
 
 
• HCl + NaOH => NaCl + H2O
 
 
 
• The neutralization of a** strong base and strong acid has a pH equal to 7.**
 
• The neutralization of a **strong base and weak acid** will be greater than 7.
 
• The neutralization of a strong acid and weak base will be less than 7.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 Process
 Conversion/Details
 
 
 
 

 Crystallization
 It is a process of conversion of liquid into a Solid crystal.
 
 

 Sublimation
 Solid directly changes into the gaseous state, without forming any liquid state
 
 

 Evaporation
 Vaporization that occurs on the surface of a liquid as it changes into the gas phase
 
 

 Condensation
 Conversion of gas to liquid.
 
 

 Decantation
 Process for the separation of mixtures of immiscible liquids or of a liquid and a solid mixture such as a suspension.

questions.question: The Election Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2021 belongs to _______ Ministry of India.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Law and Justice**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The Election Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2021 seeks to allow electoral registration officers to seek the aadhaar number of people who want to register as voters for the purpose of establishing their identity.
 
• The bill belongs to **Law and Justice**.
 
• The Election Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2021:
 
 
• Parliament on 21 December 2021 passed the Election Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2021.
 
• It seeks to link electoral rolls with Aadhaar and remove fake voters from electoral rolls.
 
• It proposes to allow election commission officials to seek Aadhaar details of registered voters on a voluntary basis and make the gender-neutral language of the Representation of the People Act, 1950.
 
• The bill will also allow officers to ask for Aadhaar numbers from persons already included in the electoral roll.
 
• Its purpose is to authenticate entries in the electoral roll and to identify the registration of the name of the same person in the electoral roll of more than one constituency or more than once in the same constituency.

questions.question: The intervention of the government whether to expand demand or reduce it constitutes the____________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**stabilisation function**____.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The government's intervention in the economy to expand or reduce demand is called a stabilization policy.
 
• This is done to prevent the economy from going into recession or experiencing high inflation.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Fiscal policy:

 
 
• ​The government can change its spending and tax levels to stimulate or slow down the economy.
 
• For example, during a recession, the government might increase spending on infrastructure projects or unemployment benefits.
 
• This would put more money into the economy and help to boost demand.
 
 
 
• Monetary policy
 
 
• The government can change the interest rates that it charges banks to borrow money.
 
• This can affect the amount of money that banks lend to businesses and consumers, which can in turn affect the level of economic activity.
 
• For example, if the government wants to stimulate the economy, it might lower interest rates.
 
• This would make it cheaper for businesses to borrow money, which would encourage them to invest and hire more workers.
 
 
 
• Stabilization: The act of stabilizing something, such as the economy.
 
 
• Stabilization policy is a complex and controversial topic.
 
• Some economists believe that the government should play a more active role in managing the economy, while others believe that the market should be allowed to operate freely.
 
• Function: The purpose or role of something.

questions.question: Which river is also known as Dakshin Ganga?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Godavari__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Godavari __River is known as 'Dakshin Ganga'.
 
• In terms of length, catchment area, and discharge, the Godavari is the largest in peninsular India.
 
• It is India's second-longest river after the Ganga.
 
• Its source is in Triambakeshwar, Maharashtra.
 
• It flows east for 1,465 kilometers (910 mi), draining the states of Maharashtra (48.6%), Telangana (18.8%), Andhra Pradesh (4.5%), Chhattisgarh (10.9%) and Odisha (5.7%).
 
• The river ultimately empties into the Bay of Bengal through an extensive network of tributaries.
 
• The Godavari basin extends over states of Maharashtra, Andhra Pradesh, Chhattisgarh and Odisha in addition to smaller parts in Madhya Pradesh, Karnataka and Union territory of Puducherry having a total area of 3,12,812 Sq.km with a maximum length and width of about 995 km and 583 km.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• Krishna

 
 
• Krishna river basin catchment area in Karnataka is 113,271 km2 
 
• It constitutes about 60% of the total catchment area of Karnataka.
 
• Krishna river basin is spread over Telangana, Andhra Pradesh and Karnataka.
 
• The Krishna river rises in western ghats in the Jor Village of Maharashtra.
 
• Total catchment area of Krishna is 258948 km2.
 
• Important tributaries of Krishna are the Ghataprabha, the Malaprabha, the Bhima, the Tungabhadra, Venna, Koyna, Panchganga, Dudhganga, and the Musi.
 
• Krishna River Basin is the fourth largest basin in India.
 
• The largest tributary of the river Krishna is Tungabhadra.
 
• Krishna is the second largest river in south Indian peninsula.
 
 
 
• Kaveri basin
 
 
• Covers the **second-largest** catchment area of Karnataka.
 
• Kaveri rises in Talakaveri in the Brahmagiri range of the western ghats of Karnataka.
 
• Important tributaries of Cauvery are Harangi, Hemavati, Kabini, Suvarnavathi and Bhavani.
 
• Cauvery is the largest river in Karnataka and called as "Ganges of South".

questions.question: The forces which act in the interior of the earth are called as ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**endogenic forces**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

Endogenic Forces:

__
 
• Endogenic forces are those internal forces that derive their strength from the earth’s interior.
 
• The forces which act in the interior of the earth are called Endogenic forces.
 
• They play a crucial role in shaping the earth's crust.
 
• The endogenic forces are mainly land-building forces.
 
• Examples: mountain-building forces, continent-building forces, earthquakes, volcanism, etc.
 
• Endogenic forces sometimes produce sudden movements, like earthquakes and volcanoes.
 
• Sudden movements cause mass destruction over the surface of the earth.
 
• These at other times produce slow movements.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3793937377c1c85871ded9776d15a4e494cf1b02a06808f706aabd74cc30a5d8.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Exogenic Forces:

 
• Exogenic forces are those forces that derive their strength from the earth’s exterior or are originated within the earth’s atmosphere.
 
• The forces that work on the surface of the earth are called Exogenic forces.
 
• Examples of forces: the wind, waves, water, etc.
 
• Examples of exogenic processes: weathering, mass movement, erosion, deposition.
 
• Exogenic forces are mainly land-wearing forces.

questions.concept: Socio - Religious Reform Movements in the 19th and 20th CE India
questions.question: Which among the following socio religious community was founded by Raja Ram Mohan Roy?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Brahmo Samaj__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Raja Ram Mohan Roy founded Brahmo Sabha in 1828, which was later renamed Brahmo Samaj.
 
 
• Its chief aim was the worship of the eternal God.
 
 
• It was against priesthood, rituals, and sacrifices.
 
 
 
• It focused on prayers, meditation, and reading the scriptures.
 
 
• It attempted to remove prejudices, negative traditions, and practices against women.
 
 
 
• It was the first intellectual reform movement in modern India.
 
 
• It led to the emergence of rationalism and enlightenment in India which indirectly contributed to the nationalist movement.
 
 
 
• It was the forerunner of all social, religious, and political movements of modern India.
 
 
• It split into two in 1866, namely Brahmo Samaj of India led by Keshub Chandra Sen, and Adi Brahmo Samaj led by Debendranath Tagore.
 
 
 
• Prominent Leaders: Debendranath Tagore, Keshub Chandra Sen, Pt. Sivnath Shastri, and Rabindranath Tagore.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

​__Some Important Socio-religious reform organisations of 19th century are-__

 
 

 
 
Name

 
 
 
Founder and Founding year

 
 
 
Purpose

 
 
 

 
 
Brahmo Samaj

 
 
 
Raja Rammohan Roy, 1828

 
 
 
 
• Hindu socio -reform movement.
 
• Advocated monotheism.
 
• Opposed sati, idolatry and superstition
 
 
 
 

 
 
Young Bengal Movement

 
 
 
Henry Vivian Derozio, 1826-31

 
 
 
 
• Opposed the vices of society.
 
• Believed in truth, freedom and reason.
 
 
 
 

 
 
Rahnumai Mazdayasnan Sabha

 
 
 
 S S Bengali, Naoroji Furdonji, Dadabhai Naoroji

 
 
 
 
• To improve social conditions of Parsis and restore the purity of Zoroastrianism.
 
 
 
 

 
 
Prarthana Samaj

 
 
 
Atmaram Pandurang, Govind Ranade, R G Bhandarkar, 1867

 
 
 
 
• Reform of society, women upliftment, abolition of caste discrimination and religious orthodoxy.
 
 
 
 

 
 
Arya Samaj

 
 
 
Dayanand Saraswati, 1875

 
 
 
 
• Revivalist movement
 
• Gave a call to “go back to vedas”.
 
• Opposed Brahmin supremacy, superstitions and idolatry.
 
 
 
 

 
 
Aligarh Movement

 
 
 
Syed Ahmed Khan

 
 
 
 
• Religious reform in Indian Islam.
 
• Emphasis on critical thinking, reasoning and rational outlook.
 
 
 
 

 
 
The Theosophical Society

 
 
 
H P Blavatsky, H S Olcott, 1875

 
 
 
 
• Religious revival and social reform
 
• Drew Inspiration from Upnishads
 
• Believed in Vedanta
 
 
 
 

 
 
Ramakrishna Mission

 
 
 
Swami Vivekananda, 1897

 
 
 
 
• Hindu religious revival.
 
• Believed in Vedanta philosophy
 
• Opposed superstitions, castism, and oppression.
 
 
 
 

 
 
The Servant of India Society

 
 
 
Gopal Krishna Gokhale, 1905

 
 
 
 
• Famine relief and upliftment of tribals.
 
• Promotion of education, removal of untouchability.

questions.question: Bahmani Monuments at Gulbarga, Karnataka represent ________ style of architecture.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Deccan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Bahmani monuments at Gulbarga, Karnataka, predominantly represent the Deccan style of architecture.
 
• The Deccan style was prominent during the period of the Bahmani Sultanate which existed from **1347 to 1527** in the Deccan region.
 
• This architectural style incorporates elements from Persian and local Deccan architecture, illustrating the diverse influences of that era.
 
• Gulbarga, the first capital of the Bahmani Sultanate, houses many important monuments such as the **Gulbarga fort and the Jama Masjid** within it, which are prime examples of the** Deccan architectural style**.
 
• The Deccan style can be seen in the simplicity of **design, use of arches, and distinct decorative elements.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mameluke**: This style pertains to the Mamluk Sultanate (Cairo), known for its architectural and cultural contributions, particularly in Egypt and the Levant. However, it is not directly connected to the Bahmani Sultanate.
 
• **Sikh**: Sikh architecture, known for its unique blend of Islamic and Hindu elements, primarily pertains to Sikh religious structures. It's not related to the Bahmani architectural style.
 
• **Nagara**: The Nagara style is a traditional Hindu architectural style that originated in northern India. It is characterized by beehive-shaped towers (shikharas) made up of layered horizontal sections, but is not associated with the Bahmani Sultanate's architectural style.

questions.question: Unemployment caused by the recession of 2008-2010 is an example of which of the following types of unemployment?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __cyclical unemployment__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Unemployment occurs when there are changes to an economy’s business cycle is termed Cyclical Unemployment.
 
• Cyclical unemployment is termed as demand deficiency i.e. unemployment starts to rise when demand falls.
 
• Causes for Cyclical Unemployment
 
 
• The decline in Demand contributes to less investment in business hence requiring fewer employees.
 
• Negative multiplier effects when demand falls this affects stores, farmers manufacturing workers,s and also those investing in transporting these goods and products which results in further affecting multiple areas.
 
• A bad Market Crash can cause a recession by instilling a loss of confidence in an economic decline in employers looking to hire and expand can be seen.
 
 
 
• Therefore, Unemployment caused by the recession of 2008-2010 is an example of Cyclical Unemployment.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Structural unemployment occurs when there is a mismatch between available jobs and available workers' talents. Many people in India struggle to find work because they lack the necessary skills, and training them is difficult due to a lack of knowledge.
 
• Frictional unemployment is the result of employment transitions within an economy where workers voluntarily leaving their jobs and new workers enter the workforce.
